thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — potential sensitive access path detected (sev=P1). Trigger: abnormal datastore read pattern flagged by DLP rules. Please assemble triage + comms. Pager: @alex, @maria

sec-eng: quick summary — automated DLP saw bulk key-value reads from a service account used by a long-running job. Initial look suggests some rows contained hashed user identifiers and a small set of metadata (no SSNs found in sampling so far). We need to confirm scope, lock down the job, and prepare a customer notice if we confirm any user data exposure.

maria: I grabbed a 1% sample and ran script `scripts/dlp/sample_expose.sh` — results show ~1200 rows with email_hash + usage_flag. No clear PII in plain text but it's still sensitive. I'll start a deeper query with filters, but I need the owner of the job and an export list of affected customer IDs. @jordan-cs can you pull customer mappings for that job?

alex: paging in — taking lead on live mitigation. Steps I'm running now: 1) pause job via infra API `POST /jobs/{id}/pause` 2) revoke service-account key (rotating) 3) snapshot datastore for forensic review. Will post outputs. handing on-call to @maria at 12:00 UTC in ~20m.

jordan-cs: copying ops playbook: customer mapping query ready. Running mapping now, ETA 10m. Will attach CSV to this thread once done. Also looping in @legal for notification guidance. :triangular_flag_on_post:

legal: thanks — preliminary ask: do not call anything "breach" yet. We'll need scope (number of customers, types of data, retention status) and a timeline before a customer notification. If exposure includes non-hashed emails or authentication tokens we escalate to mandatory disclosure.

sec-eng: to be explicit, what we need for a customer notice draft: - summary of what happened (plain language) - what data may have been accessed - timeframe - mitigation steps taken - recommended customer actions - contact for questions/legal/regulatory. I'll assemble a short template and post for review.

maria: job paused (id: job-8732). Service account key rotated. Snapshot URL: s3://forensics/1760123987/ (access restricted). Running full scan to get definitive row count and customer IDs. ETA 40m.

ops: confirmed snapshot pulled and sealed. Access audit enabled. We'll preserve logs for 90 days per incident SLA.

jordan-cs: mapping done — preliminary counts: 37 customers had rows referenced by the job. Of those, 3 are enterprise (paying tier) and 34 are self-serve. Attaching anonymized manifest: `affected_customers_manifest.csv` (internal link).

sec-eng: thanks. Maria — once you have the definitive list and whether any unhashed emails/tokens landed, we'll decide notice tier. If only hashed identifiers, prefer a scoped notification with recommended monitoring rather than full opt-in remediation.

maria: scan complete. Details: 37 customers, 0 plain-text emails, 0 tokens, 1200 rows of hashed_email + usage_flag + feature_flags. Hashes use HMAC-SHA256 with key rotated last month (we will confirm rotation history). No access to raw PII found in the snapshot.

legal: based on current scope, recommend a targeted customer notification (informational) with proactive monitoring guidance. We should still prepare a short optional status page update: `Investigating — potential access to hashed identifiers for a subset of customers; no plain-text PII detected.` Keep it high-level.

sec-eng: draft notice (please review — plain language):
```
What happened: On 2026-03-10 we detected unusual read activity from an internal job which processed customer datapoints. We paused the job and secured the environment.

What data may have been involved: Our review shows the job accessed hashed customer identifiers (HMAC-SHA256) and product usage metadata. We have not found evidence that any plain-text user identifiers or authentication credentials were exposed.

What we're doing: We paused the job, rotated the service account key, preserved forensic snapshots, and are running additional audits. We're notifying affected customers and will share recommended monitoring steps.

What you can do: No immediate action required. For customers who want additional assurance, we can provide an export of indicator hashes for correlation. Contact: security@redwood.ai
```

alex: edits: change contact to security+incidents@redwood.ai and add a sentence about timeline for follow-up (we'll update customers within 72 hours with final scope). Also add: "If you detect suspicious account activity, follow your standard incident response."

legal: minor wording change: replace "may have been involved" with "were accessed" only if we are certain. Otherwise keep tentative language. Also remove techy hash algorithm unless asked — say "hashed identifiers" not HMAC-SHA256.

sec-eng: updated draft accordingly. New draft pasted below.
```
What happened: On 2026-03-10 we detected unusual read activity from an internal job which processed customer datapoints. We paused the job and secured the environment.

What data were accessed: Our review shows the job accessed hashed customer identifiers and product usage metadata. We have not found evidence that any plain-text user identifiers or authentication credentials were exposed.

What we're doing: We paused the job, rotated the service account key, preserved forensic snapshots, and are running additional audits. We're notifying affected customers and will share recommended monitoring steps.

What you can do: No immediate action required. For customers who want additional assurance, we can provide an export of indicator hashes for correlation. Contact: security+incidents@redwood.ai
```

jordan-cs: tagging affected account managers. I'll prepare a tailored note for the three enterprise customers with suggested SLOs and support touchpoints.

emily: CS/Support — please prepare a canned response for inbound tickets: 1) Confirm we are investigating 2) Provide high-level notice 3) Escalate enterprise customers to account teams. I'll add to the shared folder `cs/templates/incident_1760123987.md`.

maria: ops — any risk of re-run or additional jobs touching the same dataset? I quieted the cron and added a deny rule to the job role. Please confirm no other cron is scheduled.

ops: confirmed — no other jobs scheduled against that dataset in prod. Added a permanent block until postmortem.

sec-eng: status page update ready (short blurb): `We are investigating unusual access to hashed identifiers by an internal job. The job has been paused and we are working to confirm scope. Affected customers are being notified directly.` Approve?

legal: approve the status page blurb. Keep it up for the next 48 hours or until final scope.

alex: handoff note — I'm offshift now. @maria you own incident comms and customer notifications. Please update the status page and send the notice to affected customers once account-specific details are attached. I'll be reachable on my mobile for urgent blockers. :phone:

maria: taking over. Will post final customer email drafts in 1h and start outbound to the three enterprise contacts for synchronous handoff.

sec-eng: thanks all. Next steps checklist (assignments): - customer manifests: @jordan-cs (done) - enterprise outreach: @jordan-cs + @emily - notice approval: @legal (in thread) - status page: @maria (pending) - postmortem owner: @maria - forensic lead: @sec-eng - SRE mitigation: @ops

onchalant-bot: Reminder: please update the incident channel thread status with any material changes.

maria: posted status page and queued customer emails. We'll follow up with a final scope update within 72 hours or sooner if new info arises. :white_check_mark:

alex: acknowledged. Closing my oncall handoff.
